subject: Re: POC/trial plan and model selection — Atlas Health
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Aditi Sharma <aditi@atlashealth.ai>, Michael Chen <mchen@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC/trial next steps — success criteria & model discussion

Hi Aditi / Michael,

Great to meet today — thanks for the time and context on Atlas Health's triage assistant use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC so we can align internally and get you up and running: 

High-level POC scope:
- Goal: Verify accuracy on clinical triage Q&A, measure latency/cost, and validate Spanish + French support for multi-lingual triage flows.
- Dataset: 1,000 representative triage prompts (we'll start with a 200 sample pilot).
- Success criteria (initial):
  - Top-1 intent accuracy >= 88% on pilot set
  - Hallucination rate < 5% on random audit
  - End-to-end median latency < 250ms (95th <= 450ms) for 512-token context
  - Cost per 1k tokens target: < $12 (goal to iterate)

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline:
1) Week 0 (this week): share POC success criteria template + access details (see attachment).
2) Week 1: Atlas shares pilot dataset + network access details. Redwood spins up trial environment and seeds models.
3) Week 2: Run automated evals & manual audit. Weekly sync with results.
4) Week 3: Iterate model selection, fallback testing, finalize recommendations.

Model selection (initial recommendation):
- Primary: Llama 2.2 Chat 13B (balanced quality for instruction-following and multilinguals).
- Fallback: Mistral 7B Instruct (quantized) for lower-latency / cost-constrained paths.
- Notes: If Spanish/French quality lags, we can test XLM-based variants or open multilingual models; we'll surface findings in Week 2.

Ownership / next steps:
- Atlas: share pilot dataset and list of endpoints to test (Aditi)
- Redwood SRE: provisioning and network checklist (Vivek)
- Redwood Solutions: evaluation scripts & metrics (Ben / Marissa)

I've attached a POC_success_criteria_template.xlsx to make it easy to fill in the details. Can you confirm you’re good with the criteria and the proposed timeline? If yes I’ll coordinate a kickoff for Monday.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Aditi Sharma <aditi@atlashealth.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Michael Chen <mchen@atlashealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC/trial next steps — success criteria & model discussion

Thanks Laura — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers from our side:

- Confirmed: the success criteria look reasonable; we'll try to hit >90% intent accuracy but 88% is a good minimum.
- Multilingual: Spanish is critical, French is nice-to-have for phase 1. We have ~300 Spanish prompts and ~80 French prompts in the pilot set.
- Compliance: we'll need an attestation about data handling during the trial (SOC2/isolated env). Can Vivek share the network/KMS requirements?

Please schedule kickoff Monday (13 Sep) 10:00am PT if that works — Michael and I will be on the call.

Thanks,
Aditi
Head of Product
Atlas Health

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Aditi Sharma <aditi@atlashealth.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC/trial next steps — model recommendations & evaluation details

Aditi — thanks, and good to have the language breakdown. A couple of technical clarifications and recommendations from Solutions: 

1) Model choices (practical starting point):
   - Primary: Llama 2.2 Chat 13B (best balance of instruction quality + multilingual performance among the open models we host).
   - Fallback (cost/latency): Mistral 7B Instruct (quantized on A10G/4xA100 densities) — expected ~30-40% lower cost with ~15-25% lower accuracy typical for domain Q&A.
   - Alternative to test if Spanish quality low: Llama 2.2 Chat 13B fine-tuned on synthetic Spanish prompts or an XLM-R based open model; we can run a quick fine-tune/test in the trial window if needed.

2) Evaluation plan details:
   - We'll run automated metrics: top-1 accuracy, BLEU/F1 for intent extraction, hallucination sampling (random 5% manual audit).
   - Latency measurements will be synthetic + real-time from your pilot traffic (we'll provide a small harness to replay).

3) Test harness + artifacts we need from Atlas:
   - Pilot dataset (CSV) with language tag column
   - Representative traffic profile (RPS, concurrency) for latency evals
   - List of endpoints/allowed IPs for the trial env

4) Owners & deliverables:
   - Ben: evaluation scripts & report (Week 2 deliverable)
   - Marissa: checklist for model prompts and edge-case tests
   - Vivek: environment & network setup (see network_requirements.pdf)

We’ll keep Llama 13B as primary initially. If we see Spanish fall-off >7-8% below English, we’ll pivot to the multilingual fallback.

-Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Aditi Sharma <aditi@atlashealth.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC/trial next steps — infra & security checklist

Hi Aditi — I’m Vivek (Redwood SRE). I’ll own the trial environment setup. A couple notes and asks: 

- Environment: we’ll provision a private trial cluster (dedicated tenancy) for Atlas with restricted egress and short-lived keys. We’ll provide a small service account and a README for network/firewall rules.
- Attachments: network_requirements.pdf includes IP allowlist, port requirements, and certificate expectations.
- Data handling: we’ll enable in-flight TLS and customer-managed KMS for any uploaded artifacts; for the trial we can enable audit logging and a temporary retention policy (30 days) per your compliance ask. Please confirm if 30 days is acceptable for the pilot or if you require longer.

Action items for Atlas:
- Share pilot CSV + sample PII redaction notes (Aditi)
- Provide IPs for allowlist and Slack contact for emergency access

I’ll start provisioning once we have the allowlist and a signed trial agreement (DocuSign link below).

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Aditi Sharma <aditi@atlashealth.ai>

Laura / team — thank you. Confirming the plan and timeline: kickoff Monday 13 Sep 2026 at 10:00am PT works for us (we’ll assume the Monday referenced was intended as 13 Sep).

Quick checklist: 
- We’ll upload the pilot CSV to the Drive folder you shared by EOD today (contains 580 English, 300 Spanish, 80 French rows).
- IP allowlist / procurement contact will be shared by Michael this afternoon.
- SOC2 attestation: we’re OK with 30 day trial retention for now; please include the attestation text in the DocuSign.

Ben — look forward to the Week 2 evaluation report. Vivek — we’ll send the allowlist + contact. Laura — thanks for coordinating; please send calendar invite for the kickoff.
